title: Backlog.md-to-Quest migration skill in the opum-quest plugin
description: Operator instruction 2026-10-02, relayed via opum-doc seq 164 (opum-agent OPAG-1089): "add a claude skill to the quest skill in the marketplace to do the supported migrations from claude code itslef (backlog.md to quest)". Design is opum-docs: docs/reference/pane-full-screen-and-quest-migration-skill-design.md at opum-ai/opum-doc main 945d0ae2, section 2. Ships skills/migrate-from-backlog/SKILL.md in the opum-quest plugin, beside the existing quest skill, driven from inside Claude Code. Lands on dev with a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

acceptanceCriteria.text: skills/migrate-from-backlog/SKILL.md ships in the opum-quest plugin and triggers on migration intent, and skills/quest/SKILL.md carries a one-line pointer to it

The skill drives quest migration backlog preview, apply, status and rollback, choosing ids and approving the apply each through AskUserQuestion, with the apply write recorded as the person who approved it: --actor <id> --actor-kind human
The skill never deletes backlog/, never commits, and never applies a digest other than the one just previewed; each of those three refusals is asserted in a test with a positive control beside it

Against a throwaway fixture repository carrying a small backlog/, a test proves preview writes nothing to the tree, apply with a stale digest is refused, status reports the applied mappings, and rollback removes the migrated records, leaves backlog/ untouched, and keeps the rolled-back receipt
The skill tells the person to commit the migrated records through the repository normal branch-and-PR flow rather than doing it for them

plan: 1. Read the quest skill, the migration guides, and how the plugin ships skills
2. Write skills/migrate-from-backlog/SKILL.md driving preview, apply, status and rollback
3. Add the one-line pointer from the quest skill
4. Fixture tests: preview writes nothing, a stale digest is refused, status reports, rollback restores, each beside a positive control
5. CHANGELOG under Unreleased, bun run check, open the PR
implementationNotes:
QCLI-436 BUILT, 2026-10-02, design read by ref at opum-doc main 945d0ae2 section 2. All five acceptance criteria met, with AC4's "rollback restores the pre-apply tree" met in the sense measured and qualified below rather than literally.

WHAT LANDED. skills/migrate-from-backlog/SKILL.md ships in the opum-quest plugin: detect both sides (and stop for `quest init` when there is no workspace), choose ids through AskUserQuestion, preview and show the counts, mappings and digest, apply only the digest just previewed after a second AskUserQuestion with the approving person as --actor-kind human (DEC-134), verify with status and `quest check`, hand the commit to the repository's own branch-and-PR flow, and roll back behind a third AskUserQuestion. It never deletes backlog/, never commits, and never applies a digest other than the one just previewed. test/qcli436-migrate-from-backlog-skill.test.ts runs the lifecycle against a throwaway repository with a two-record backlog/.

THREE MEASUREMENTS THAT CONTRADICT AN ASSUMPTION, each found by running rather than reading.

1. --source NAMES A DIRECTORY, NOT A PROJECT. The help says `--source <project>`, and passing a bare name fails with `ENOENT ... lstat 'demo'`: the value is used as a path and realpath'd. The skill now says so in its own words -- "a path the person names" -- rather than repeating the help text's noun.

2. A STALE DIGEST IS REFUSED AS A DIGEST MISMATCH, NOT A FINGERPRINT CONFLICT. The design's flow implies the source-changed-since-preview case, and src/domain/migration/migration.ts does carry `migration_source_fingerprint_conflict` for it. But `apply` RE-DERIVES the plan from the source as it now stands before asserting, so with the source moved the approved digest no longer matches the plan it rebuilt and the run fails earlier, at `migration_approval_digest_mismatch`. Both refuse the write; the test asserts the one measured, with the reason in a comment, rather than the one I predicted.

3. ROLLBACK DOES NOT RESTORE THE TREE BYTE-FOR-BYTE, and this is the one worth a decision. AC4 and the design both say "rollback restores the pre-apply tree". Measured: it restores the RECORDS -- the migrated .quest/tasks/*.json are gone -- but it leaves its own receipt at .quest/migrations/backlog/<digest>.json, marked `"state":"rolled-back"`, plus an empty .quest/planning.json. Neither is a record and neither is something rollback should take away: the receipt is exactly how `status --digest` can still answer after a rollback. So the test asserts what is true and useful -- every file that existed before still exists with identical contents (including the untouched backlog/ source), no migrated record remains, and exactly one receipt does -- instead of a whole-tree equality that fails. If the operator wants the literal reading, it is a CLI change, not a skill change, and it would cost `status` its answer after a rollback. Reporting rather than settling.

THE UNREQUESTED CROSS-REPO EFFECT, which the orchestrator should know before this ships. skills/quest/SKILL.md is GENERATED: QCLI-372 holds the committed plugin copy byte-equal to questSkillDoc("plugin") and the repo variant equal to questSkillDoc("repo"), the two differing only in their provenance sentence. So the one-line pointer could not be added to the plugin file alone -- putting it there reddened test/qcli372-plugin-skill-drift.test.ts, which is that gate working as designed. It went into the generator in src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts instead, and both variants carry it. Consequence: every workspace running `quest agents --check` sees drift once it installs a quest that has this, until it runs `quest agents --update-instructions`. That is the ordinary path for any generated-content change and the managed block is version-stamped anyway, but it is a fleet-visible effect of a skill edit and it was not in the brief.

TESTS AND THE PROOF THEY REJECT. Six new tests. Mutations, each reddening a predicted subset: pointing the fixture's records at a folder preview does not read reddens 5 of 6 (every CLI test, "preview writes nothing" included -- which is the point, since an absence assertion that survives an unreadable source is the one that certifies nothing), removing the never-commits line reddens 1, and removing the pointer from the quest skill reddens 1. A full `bun run check` under the pinned bun 1.4.2 exits 0: repository suite 1082 pass / 0 fail, mod suite 21 pass / 0 fail.

DEPENDENCIES UNCHANGED: no binary source, no package version, no lockfile. Note that the CHANGELOG entry and this task's bookkeeping are the only non-skill changes; the six committed platform packages on #486 are still valid.
finalSummary:
The opum-quest plugin now ships a migrate-from-backlog skill, from the operator's instruction via opum-doc seq 164: it drives quest migration backlog through preview, apply, status and rollback from inside Claude Code, stops at each write for the person to approve with AskUserQuestion -- once to choose whether the records keep Backlog's own ids or take Quest's, once to approve the exact digest just previewed, once to confirm a rollback -- records the apply as the approving person (--actor-kind human, DEC-134), and hands the commit to the repository's own branch-and-PR flow. It never deletes backlog/, never commits, and never applies a digest other than the one just previewed.

Landed on dev by squash merge as opum-ai/quest-cli#490 at bea76848. Verification: bun run check exit 0 under the pinned bun 1.4.2 -- repository suite 1082 pass / 0 fail, mod suite 21 pass / 0 fail. Six new tests in test/qcli436-migrate-from-backlog-skill.test.ts run the lifecycle against a throwaway repository with a small backlog/, and every absence asserted -- preview writes nothing, a stale digest is not applied, rollback gives the records back -- is checked beside a positive control in the same run, because an absence assertion that survives an unreadable source certifies nothing. Mutation-tested: pointing the fixture at a folder preview does not read reddens 5 of 6, removing the never-commits line reddens 1, removing the pointer reddens 1.

Three measurements contradicted an assumption and are recorded on the task: --source names a directory rather than a project (filed as QCLI-437, unfixed pending a ruling because renaming the placeholder also renames the positional in quest manifest --json); a stale digest is refused as migration_approval_digest_mismatch rather than the fingerprint conflict, because apply re-derives the plan before asserting; and rollback restores the records rather than the tree byte-for-byte, leaving its own receipt and an empty planning.json.

That last one was routed and came back as a design defect, not a build defect. opum-doc seq 167 (design corrected at opum-doc#624, main 080b63a) withdrew DEC-139 and amended AC4 to the measured behaviour, which the test already asserted -- so this closing carries no code change for it.

One effect beyond this repository, recorded on QCLI-433 as a release note: the quest skill file is generated (QCLI-372 holds the committed copy byte-equal to questSkillDoc("plugin")), so the one-line pointer had to go into the generator and both variants carry it. A workspace installing 0.13.0 will therefore see quest agents --check report drift until it runs quest agents --update-instructions.
